- The fungus's own situation (§5.2): load, hostActivity, ground, contact, groomed, apart = 648 possible; a run meets far fewer.
- The player's levers on the policy (§5.1): strain (which interventions/caps exist), aim (goal in words), menu (options on/off), thresholds (tune the local rule). Wire at least the strain gate (cull) and the menu here.
- Jev for the fungus lane: cached per fungal situation under the player's aim, in its own lane (never in an ant request). Can follow once the local rule plays well — file as a follow-up if not done here.

Tests: the ant request for an infected host is byte-identical to a healthy ant's in the same perceived situation (the policy never enters an ant request); a cull-less strain never yields a lethal intervention.

description:
docs/fungus-policy.md §2, §4.A, §8 (piece 2). Depends on 1a.

One distortion step between #sense (colony.ts:323) and BOTH the situation (colony.ts:415) AND steering — they must read the same bent sensors, or the host decides by one world and walks in another (§6 failure mode 5).

title: Fungus 1a: infection state, contact spread, grooming, spore brush
description:
docs/fungus-policy.md §4.S, §5.1, §8 (piece 1). The foundation; blocks 1b/1c/1d.

- Two typed arrays on the ant structure of arrays (web/src/colony/colony.ts): `load` (Float32, 0..1) and `expr` (Uint8, the intervention running in that host; just carried for now).
- S1 Transmission: each tick a host gains β × Σ load of ants in its 3×3 cells, across BOTH colonies — reuse the neighbourhood battle.ts already scans with block sums (CountGrid). Lives in game.ts (it sees both colonies), like resolveFights.
- Grooming + decay: a visible host next to healthy nestmates loses load (and the groomer gains a small dose → later resistance); load decays slowly, or not at all for a persistent strain.
- S2 Visibility: how much load shows (a strain param), the hook grooming/rejection read.
- W3 Spore brush: a third brush beside lure/alarm (useColony.ts:29, BRUSHES) that raises load on ground + ants in the stroke with the loaded strain. It does NOT pick interventions.

Tests (node --test): a loaded ant among clean ants raises their load; an isolated ant is unchanged; grooming lowers visible load; transmission is symmetric across colonies.

title: MR: fungus 1 — the player is the fungus (perceived-state mechanics)
description:
First slice of the fungus game (docs/fungus-policy.md §8). The player is the fungus and nothing else: it never decides for an ant. Each colony keeps its own policy, doctrine, 1,296 situations and cache unchanged. The fungus bends a host's PERCEIVED state and acts through emission, body and spread levers; the host's own policy then chooses from that bent state. Win via a unity meter (§1), not won/lost.

title: Cached 'return' can park ants at the nest (situation can't tell an ant is already home)
description: Review of #3 (plausible, depends on live Jev). An ant that just put food down is asked as return|fresh|...|home strong; a cached 'return' keeps it at the nest forever (never tired: since resets there). Simulated: food stored stalls at ~half. An atNest field alone did not fix it (the other branch's live check: Jev still said return at the nest in 10 situations). Fix: a mechanic, or a new meaning for 'return'.

title: A save on a tick with a fight death diverges on reload
description: Every game, not only one world. title: Tiredness as a sensed body state, not a timer that only the hole resets
description:
Today "tired" is one timer: `since` (seconds since the ant last found food, put a load down, or stood in its hole's radius) over `patience × clock`. Local rule: tired → return. Behaviour MR 2 (ja-mz7, PRD §43) showed how far this is from an ant's state:

- **Underground nothing resets it.** In the side view an ant inside the nest never passes the hole's radius, so every inside worker becomes "tired" within about a minute, and a tired forager that goes home stays tired for good. The colony's tired foragers retire inside. When MR 2 rested them on arrival, they went out again, more food came in than the porters could move, and it piled up at reception (A8). The economy has come to depend on that artefact.
- **Rest is instant or never.** The hole resets the timer in one tick; the royal chamber never does. Real foragers return after an unsuccessful bout and may stay in the nest before the next excursion.
- **It counts the wrong thing.** Finding food, putting down spoil, or a fight all reset it the same way. A harvester forager's trip length is set by its search time: it searches, and goes home at once when it finds a seed. Tiredness should measure an *unsuccessful* search: time out without food, trail contact or a successful return.
- **Jev doesn't read it as meaning anything.** Warlike sends tired ants out exploring or following (ja-3sy), which is the mill that "tired → return" exists to break. The legend never says why tiredness matters.
- **It is not sensed.** Per docs/vision.md, an ant's state should come from its own body. Candidates: crop fill or energy; a giving-up time on an unsuccessful search (Cataglyphis searches, then gives up and follows nest cues); rest that accrues inside the nest at a rate, not by a reset.

1. A research note with primary sources (giving-up times, rest between bouts, trip structure: Gordon on Pogonomyrmex, Wehner on Cataglyphis, Formica giving-up time by food type), as docs/vision.md requires for a new sense.
2. Replace `since` with a body state that drains while searching unsuccessfully and refills while resting inside (a rate, not a reset). Make sure inside workers aren't "tired" by construction.
3. Retune against A3 (depletion: tired is what breaks mills), A5 (regulation: rest between bouts is activation, MR 5) and A8, plus the hour-long economy run. Watch the economy's knife-edge (ja-xu6), which currently leans on retired foragers.
4. Say in the mode legend what tired means for the colony.

Sources found so far (abstract and snippet level, **unverified**):
- Pinter-Wollman et al. 2013 (red harvester trip duration set by search time, not distance), PLoS ONE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3540075
- Cataglyphis search under nest-position uncertainty, J. Exp. Biol. 209:3545: https://cob.silverchair.com/jeb/article-pdf/209/18/3545/1256157/3545.pdf
- Formica giving-up time by food type, Behav. Ecol. 19:217: https://ideas.repec.org/a/oup/beheco/v19y2008i1p217-222.html

title: Doctrine is inherited: change a colony's policy only by a fraction, and only through a new queen sent out to found a colony
description:
Idea (owner, 2026-11-05). Today a colony's doctrine (the ants' policy words Jev reads) can be rewritten at any moment, in the side panel or the Learn drawer's Policy tab, and every ant reconsiders at once. Instead, a colony's policy should be heritable, not steerable:

- A living colony's doctrine is fixed: you can't rewrite it for the ants already there.
- A change applies only to a NEW colony, founded by a queen the colony sends out (nuptial flight, or budding as in Pharaoh ants).
- Even then, the change is limited to some fraction of the policy: the daughter's doctrine is the mother's, varied by at most a set amount (a mutation budget), not a free rewrite.

Open questions to settle before building:
- What 'a fraction' means for words Jev reads: edit distance or share of sentences changed; preset-to-preset steps; or a doctrine made of weighted clauses where only weights move by up to x%.
- Who sends the queen and when: a colony at its cap with a full larder (the strategist's 'larder full, ants many'), or a player action with a cost.
- Where the new colony goes and how it starts (a few workers, its own nest in the side view); interaction with ja-8fd.1 (several queens), ja-1vg.1 (adoption) and docs/queens-and-merging.md.
- How it fits the vision (docs/vision.md): the player is the fungus, and doctrines are each colony's nature, a scenario setting. Inheritance makes policy change evolutionary, which suits that.
- Jev cost: each new doctrine is a new cache context, so every founding re-asks its situations (about $0.0015 per doctrine retune at today's ~769 tokens per question).

Research note first (queens-and-merging.md covers founding and budding in part): colony founding modes, and how much of a colony's behaviour is heritable.

In scripts/raids.mjs runs, 150–375 of the raiding colony's dead lie far out at 450 s. Decide whether undertakers walk farther out after a fight (calm, no stance raid), or whether rotting in the field is the design.

title: Behaviour MR 6: roles and age
description: docs/PRD.md §14 (plan: behaviours as responses to stimuli, tuned by offline assays). Per-ant response thresholds and age-based jobs (inside → entrance → forager). Prepares castes (MR 8/11). Targets: A5, A8.

title: Fungus palette and brush (skills)
description: docs/PRD.md §14 (plan: behaviours as responses to stimuli, tuned by offline assays). Record a behaviour from a few ants (situation + action), paint it as a skill invoked on ants in a place; reinforce per (place/situation, skill) like a contextual bandit from deliveries there. Offline: a brush is a scripted runGame event; the assay measures whether the behaviour appears where painted.

title: Queen adoption: polygyne colonies accept mated queens within tolerance
description: docs/queens-and-merging.md §3.2. Needs nuptial flights (lifetime layer). Accept when species allows several queens and her odour is within the nest odour's tolerance.

title: Orphans merging: an orphaned colony's workers defect to a tolerated neighbour (unification route)
description: docs/queens-and-merging.md §3.3–3.4. Defection on mutual tolerance (allied contact), walk to host's hole, change colony (spawn in host copying age/load/strain, kill without corpse); brood carried across; Outcome 'merged' counts as unified. Measure time from orphaning to last defector, share arriving.
notes: Needs (review of the design, docs/queens-and-merging.md §3.3): Colony.adopt/leave instead of spawn/kill; Brood items moved between colonies; mutual calm tolerance check (fungus 'allied' is one-way, infected-only); per-colony raid targets for the walk; host maxAnts cap; 'merged' outcome ahead of fallen().

title: Several queens per colony: Colony.queens[], per-species queens trait
description: docs/queens-and-merging.md §3.1. Colony.queen → queens[]; orphaned = all dead; one royal chamber per queen; species trait queens: one | several (fire ant: polygyne flag). One-queen colonies unchanged. Measure growth vs one queen; crown orphaning time with two.

title: Fungus crown: reachable now (queen dies 19–53 s after a Bloom stroke at the hole); should it wait?
description: Review of #27: as built in nest slice 8, crown acted only from a high load (≥ 0.7), which grooming takes Bloom's hosts below within ~8 s; no queen ever died in a game, and PRD §37's 12–23 s could not be reproduced (no harness was committed). The nest fix-up (PRD §39) makes crown act at any load, at CROWN_RATE (0.05) × the host's load a second, for the queen and each brood item a host is by. Harness: scripts/crown.mjs (app setup, 600 + 600 ants, the UI brush: radius 3, spores 2, dose 0.15; scripted policy: crown wherever a Bloom host is in its own chamber). A 6-event stroke across colony 1's hole at 60 s: the queen dies 19 / 26 / 53 s later (seeds 1–3), 66–104 brood killed, births 43 / 22 / 52 against ~150–240 in the other colony. The same stroke along the royal chamber: 4–34 s (and 4–34 s too at a fifth of the rate, since many hosts are by her: rate alone barely paces it). Open, the owner's: should crown wait for something (a host's time by the queen, her guards), or is a quick orphaning the lethal play's point?

title: Side view: measure the midden as a boundary once raids carry across to the rival's nest
description: Nest slice 7 (PRD §36): raiders now walk the ground and turn back from the rival's midden (unit test), but in full games raids are fought out near the raiders' own nest and seldom come within 20 columns of the rival's hole in 5 minutes, so the boundary effect is unmeasured. Related: ja-jwy (raid paths).
close_reason: Measured in slice 7's review fixes (PRD §36): raids now carry across; the rival's midden cuts raiders within 20 columns of its hole from 11–54 to ~2 on seeds 1 and 3.

title: Phase 6: roles and age
description: Per-ant response thresholds and age-based jobs (inside -> entrance -> forager); prepares castes (ja-8fd, ja-jhd). Assays A5, A8.
close_reason: Duplicate of ja-6df (claude/fungus-behavior-palette-qg2n9p, merged 2026-11-02; that branch's beads are canonical)

title: Nest 9: design for MR 8: several queens, adoption, orphans merging (a unification route)
description: Design: docs/nest-and-home.md (PRD §28). Builds on the side view (mr13–15). Polygyny and queen adoption per species (ja-8fd). Speculative unification path: an orphaned colony merging into a neighbour it tolerates (same odour via Garden). Design note only.
close_reason: Design note docs/queens-and-merging.md (nest slice 9, PRD §38); follow-ups filed under ja-8fd and ja-1vg.

title: Nest 6: age and zoning: young nurse deep, old forage
description: Design: docs/nest-and-home.md (PRD §28). Builds on the side view (mr13–15). Per-ant age; young near queen and brood, middle dig and carry, oldest forage (Tschinkel). Age as a perception/assignment input; prerequisite for castes (ja-jhd). Measure: where ants are by age.
close_reason: Built (PRD §35): age bands (young nurse deep, never out; middle dig and carry, out when foragers are short; old forage, climb out); young 14-15 rows deep, old 8-10; food -4%

title: Nest 7: the midden: refuse and corpses carried out, a boundary
description: Design: docs/nest-and-home.md (PRD §28). Builds on the side view (mr13–15). Corpses (later spent garden) carried to a midden at the mound's edge (harvesters) or a deep chamber (Atta cephalotes). Middens deter other ants (P. badius). Measure: corpses cleared; effect on raids.
close_reason: Built (PRD §36): corpses carried to a surface midden past the mound (cleared within ~2 min); midden mark; raids made to work on the ground and raiders turn back from the rival's midden (unit test); in-game boundary effect not yet measurable

title: Nest 5: food flow: reception at the top, stores deep, fed to brood and queen
description: Design: docs/nest-and-home.md (PRD §28). Builds on the side view (mr13–15). Foragers drop in reception (harvester ants: top chambers), inside workers carry down to store (granaries 20–80 cm, Tschinkel & Kwapich), then to brood and queen. stored/larder become food lying in chambers. Measure: food home; carries per food.
close_reason: Built (PRD §34): food lies in chambers; foragers to reception, porters to wanted chambers (brood, queen) then stores; queen and larvae eat what lies by them; 1.3 porter trips per food

title: Cull's odour push depends on which side of 0.5 the nest's odour has drifted to
description: PR #7 review, unconfirmed. Recognition.step pushes a culled host's odour by 0.5 away from its nest's odour, toward the far side; zero if the nest is exactly 0.5. After Garden drifts the nests (e.g. 0.3 / 0.7), a culled host lands within tolerance of the other nest, so 'both colonies take it for a stranger' no longer holds. Push to the band farthest from every nest, or define the weapon by distance from every colony.

title: ColonyJev: 429 re-queue lost after a doctrine switch leaves ants on the local rule
description: PR #7 review, unconfirmed. On 429 the re-queue is dropped when the lane's context changed or the lane is orphaned; another colony's lane on the old context had already removed the item and nothing calls reconsider, so those ants stay local until some other reply lands. Self-heals on any later reply.
close_reason: Fixed on branch claude/fungus-behavior-palette-qg2n9p, commit cd5cd4b: a 429 batch is re-queued into every current lane asking under its context (not only the sender, which may be orphaned or recontexted). Test: busy after a new game.

title: Fungus lane may starve: #cycle fills the in-flight slots in fixed order, fungus last
description: PR #7 review, unconfirmed. ColonyJev.#cycle fills the 2 in-flight slots lane by lane (colony 0 stances, modes, colony 1 ..., fungus last). While mode queues refill early in a game, the fungus lane (and colony 1 under its own doctrine) may wait several cycles. Measure queue age per lane; round-robin if it matters.
close_reason: Fixed on branch claude/fungus-behavior-palette-qg2n9p, commit cd5cd4b: #cycle takes one batch per lane per pass and rotates the starting lane each cycle. Test: with batch 1 and one slot, the fungus is asked among the first 4 requests instead of after 27 mode questions. Queue age not measured live.

title: Hex grid tick cost: +23% underground / +33% open vs MR7
description: MR8 bench (1200+1200 ants): underground 3.7 vs 3.0 ms, open 5.2 vs 3.9 ms. Spread over the 6-neighbour scent stencil (#edgeCell via #at per neighbour), hex disc windows in #enemyHeading / resolveFights, tunnel checks. Ideas: specialised border loops for the 6 stencil, cache ant cells for fights in Game, precomputed neighbour index tables per parity.

title: Endless map: generate soil, chambers and food per chunk as the colony digs outward
description: World generation is position-pure per chunk (heightAt / chamberAt), but nest/food placement and the reachability prune are whole-map. For the endless map (lifetime game), generate a chunk's soil and food when a tunnel reaches its edge, with placement rules that only look at that chunk and its neighbours; reachability by digging is automatic underground (no rock seals: check per chunk).

title: Pellet scent and Atta-like backfill (MR11 backfills unused dead ends: 0.6% of dug soil)
description: MR11: pellet carriers >3 s into a trip fill a neighbouring unused dead end (no food, no food/home scent, no ant, not by the nest; stub = 1-2 adjacent open neighbours). Measured 0.6% of dug soil backfilled (harvester ants ~2.5%; Atta most). Without the 3 s wait carriers refilled their own just-dug cell (dig-fill churn, 53%, economy down). Next: pellets laying a building scent (Khuong 2016) to draw digging; a slower 'unused' test (scent fading over minutes) for Atta-like colonies; species parameter.
close_reason: MR12: leaf-cutter backfill. Unused judged against the path (scent < 0.5x the carrier's cell, never above it), fillable = any open cell whose open neighbours form one run (chamber edges, wide-tunnel sides, dead ends; never cuts a passage), carriers turn into stale branches and fill them from the tip, fresh pellets draw more (building scent, tau 60 s). First cut measured 53.3% refilled, but 38-46% of all digs re-dug filled cells. Review fixes: filled cells not dug for 600 s, cells dug in the last 200 s not filled, carriers never refill their own dig, stale turn-ins never reverse. Seeds 1-5, 600 s: 27% of dug soil refilled with no re-digs, food home ~940/colony (first cut ~980, MR11 ~1,080). PRD 26.

title: Co-infection: strains compete inside a host (today the first strain holds it)
description: fungus.ts: a host keeps the strain that infected it first; another strain's contact or brush dose adds load under the first strain's traits. Fine while there are two strains and one brush, but painting Lockpick into a Bloom-infected colony silently does nothing strain-wise. Options: per-strain load (a small array per ant), or strain replacement when the incoming strain's load share passes a threshold. Changes the per-ant state size; measure colony-bench worst case before and after.

title: A Start reply that lands after the page unmounts leaves the run open (picture and colony Jev clients)
description: Round 3 of the review of #2: click Colony while Start's POST /api/run is still waiting; at unmount the phase is idle so no stop is sent; when the reply lands start() sets running and starts timers on the disposed scheduler (2 /api/jev calls in 4 s, answers never saved). Fix: a #disposed flag that start() checks after its await (send a stop and return). Same pattern in ColonyJev.start.
close_reason: Fixed on branch claude/fungus-behavior-palette-qg2n9p, commit cd5cd4b: #disposed flag in ColonyJev and JevScheduler; a Start reply after dispose opens no run, starts no timers, and POSTs stop. Tests in colonyJev.test.ts and jevScheduler.test.ts fail on the old code.

title: Move the field's gesture logic into a pure, tested module
description: Review of #6. Click vs drag slop (use net displacement, not total path), pick reach, pinch hand-off, what ends a follow, fitted/zoomedIn flags, minimap hit test, brush scale: all inside ColonyField.tsx with no tests.

title: Keyboard access to following an ant and to the minimap
description: Review of #6. Arrows/WASD/+/-/0/n cover the camera; there is no keyboard way to pick an ant (e.g. cycle nearest ants with Tab/F) or to use the minimap.

title: The player's colony ticks first and wins every contested food pickup
description: Review of #4. game.ts ticks colonies in order. Alternate the order per tick, or resolve pickups after both have moved.

title: World generation may favour the player (nest central, rival at the edge of reach)
description: Review of #4: in a 10-seed sweep the player won 4, the rival led 2. Measure food within walking distance of each nest and balance placement.

title: Validate cached Jev answers loaded from localStorage (modes and stances); make the loader testable
description: Reviews of #3/#4. Any string is accepted as a Mode/Stance; a bad value becomes a permanent hit and STANCES.indexOf(-1) would corrupt encode. Filter per lane; move the loader out of the React hook so node --test covers it; consider pruning old custom-doctrine keys and two tabs overwriting each other.
close_reason: Fixed on branch claude/fungus-behavior-palette-qg2n9p, commit cd5cd4b: stored answers kept only if the lane could have given them (colonyJev.validAnswer); loader moved to ui/cacheStore.ts with tests; saves merge with what another tab stored. Pruning old custom-doctrine keys not done.

title: avoid() treats rock or the map edge (-1) as the weakest alarm, steering ants into walls
description: Review of #3. Count rock/edge as +Infinity (or clamp to 0) when choosing the least-alarmed sensor.
close_reason: avoid() reads rock/edge as the most alarm (MR 4, PRD 46.3)

title: Keep bd across cloud sessions: add it to the environment setup script
description: Containers are ephemeral. Add to the environment's setup script: apt-get install -y libicu-dev && (command -v bd || go install github.com/steveyegge/beads/cmd/bd@v1.3.2). Owner: the user (environment settings).

title: MR 13: world events and fungus powers
description: Rain/flood/drought, antlion pits, bird, myrmecophile beetle; unlockable fungus brushes (propaganda, rain, decoy food, spore wall); flight/tournament spectacle; documentary follow-cam; time-lapse GIF export.

title: MR 11: castes and species wave 2
description: Per-ant caste; traits/*.ts hooks. Leafcutter (fungus garden, stridulation), weaver (territory marks), harvester (granary, return-rate), big-headed ant (enemy specification, absconding). Caste in the situation only for polymorphic species (×2).

title: MR 12: species wave 3, unusual life histories
description: Army ant (nomadic bivouac), Argentine ant (supercolony alliance), honeypot ant (repletes, tournaments), slave-maker (brood raids, propaganda). Tournament/raid strategist lane.

title: Debounce CacheStore.save (rewrites the whole cache after every reply)
description: docs/refactor.md S6.4.
acceptance_criteria: At most one write per second under load.

title: Day and night in the game
description: No day/night cycle exists. Needed first by ja-lsu (entrances sealed at night, docs/entrances.md §3); would also bear on ant activity rhythms and, in one world, on sunlight on the surface (ja-6ip).

title: Entrances closed at night, and plugged by rivals
description: docs/entrances.md §3: harvester ants seal their entrances at night (P. occidentalis, AntWiki, secondary; P. barbatus, Wikipedia, secondary) and reopen them; Novomessor cockerelli plugs P. barbatus entrances, delaying its foraging (Gordon 1988, Oecologia 75:114). Needs day and night in the game first (ja-0qs). Would give foragers caught outside a reason to hurry home and raiders a defence to dig through.

title: Bring the broad notes up to the plan check: In the game paragraphs, Sources sections
description: check-plan.sh (adding-mechanics skill) still reports 'In the game' missing for ant-communication.md, nest-and-home.md, fungus-policy.md and one-world.md, and Sources missing for nest-and-home.md (inline links) and one-world.md (design, no papers). They carry the same content in their own shape (Implications, The model). Either add In the game paragraphs / a Sources list, or teach check-plan.sh a 'broad note' or 'design note' kind.
acceptance_criteria: check-plan.sh passes the Play/In the game/Sources checks for all 12 notes, or skips them for a declared note kind with a test in scripts/test.sh.

title: Daily Jev budget rolls at UTC midnight; consider the owner's local day
description: PR #42 re-review nit (S8). web/server/ledger.ts dayOf() uses the UTC date, so the budget resets around 4-5 pm Pacific. If the owner prefers, use the server's local date (or a JEV_BUDGET_TZ setting). Update the ledger tests (DAY constants) and PRD 50.11.

title: A deterministic test for the chamber-join re-check in #chamberDug
description: F2 (PRD §41) re-checks a chamber face when it is dug (joining another chamber, its chamber's rows, depth) and clears stale faces on a mode change and in #homeAfresh (review of #21: joins at 73 s and 352 s on seed 5, two colonies, app map). The two-colony test in chambers.test.ts doesn't fail with the re-check reverted: no join happened in 8 small two-colony worlds over 400 s, nor on the app map's seeds 5 and 1 over 600 s with it reverted. Build a direct test: aim a face for chamber A, grow chamber B beside it, then let the dig finish.

title: Worker-laid males in orphaned colonies
description: docs/queens-and-merging.md §3.5. Orphaned workers lay male eggs; only matters with flights and lineage.

title: Fungus.configure alone changes the gate's menu without telling Jev
description: PR #7 review. React wiring calls both Fungus.configure and ColonyJev.setMenu; scripts or tests calling configure alone get Jev asked under a different menu than the gate runs. Make the menu one source (e.g. ColonyJev reads fungus.menu, or configure notifies).

title: ColonyJev: a colony without its own doctrine follows colony 0's only at the next game
description: PR #7 review. attachColonies gives colony k #doctrines[k] ?? #doctrines[0] without storing it; setDoctrineFor(0) later leaves colony k on the old words until the next attach. The UI always sets both; API callers and scripts hit it.
close_reason: Fixed on branch claude/fungus-behavior-palette-qg2n9p, commit cd5cd4b: setDoctrineFor(0) also recontexts every colony with no doctrine of its own.

title: Spore counter counts cells too faint to see
description: The Fungus panel's "spores N cells" counts every cell above the 1e-3 the fungus forgets spores at, but the field draws spores only above ~0.06 (sp > 0.02 of 3). After a whole-map sweep it read "119,925 cells" with nothing violet on the ground. Count cells at or above the drawn threshold (a pass over #sporeCells), or show the total spores instead of a cell count.

title: Minimap: show spores and infected ants
description: ColonyField's minimap (paintMini) draws ground, food and both colonies' ants, but not the fungus: spore cells and infected ants only show in the main view. Tint infected ants in --spore on the minimap and wash spore cells, so the player sees spread across the whole map.

title: Small maps: some seeds place no food (under ~100×60)
description: Round 2 review of #5: at 100×60 seed 15 and 64×64 seed 12 have no food; at 40×30 the fallback rival nest can be 8 cells from the player's. The default 512×320 (and 1024×640) is clean. Scale patch density/min distance to small maps or guarantee at least one patch.

title: PRD §9 numbers don't reproduce with the UI's seeding
description: Review of #2: food home 32-92 % (PRD 49-86 %), seed 1 at 60 s 866 (PRD 1,077), situations seen 54-57 (PRD ~30), mode choices 3,300-4,200/s early (PRD 500-2,000). State the RNG used or update the numbers.
notes: Partly addressed by behaviour MR 0: gameRng(seed, generation) is now the one scheme for the page and experiment.ts, so new numbers (PRD §14) reproduce on the page. colony-cost/colony-bench and older tests still seed their own way; §9 figures stay as measured.
close_reason: gameRng is the one seeding scheme (page, runGame, colony-cost --side, colony-live), PR #31; §9's old figures stay as measured

title: Seed input: clearing the field forces 1 and every keystroke regenerates the world
description: Review of #2. Commit the seed on blur/Enter; allow an empty field while typing.

title: Follow card: record who decided when the ant chose, not at render time
description: Review of #6. explain(q) runs at render; while paused, pressing Stop Jev relabels a Jev-decided ant as 'local rule'. Record the deciding source on the colony when the policy answers.

title: Small edge cases in the game outcome and enemy counts
description: Review of #4: both colonies beaten in the same tick shows 'lost' (a draw?); the enemy grid and enemiesNearNest count ants killed this tick for one tick.

title: Field goes soft when the window moves to a screen with a different DPR
description: ColonyField sizes its canvas from devicePixelRatio only on ResizeObserver; moving between monitors changes DPR without a CSS resize, so the picture is blurry until the next resize. Already so before MR 6. Fix: also listen to matchMedia('(resolution: Xdppx)') changes.
